The latter may test whether the signed count sectors can eventually have one sign, without assuming noncollision.

The large-count relation looks viable. The source-weighted radius appears to concentrate near \(a_j\), defined by \(a_j e^{4a_j}=j/(2\pi)\), making the normalized signed count approach \(\cos(k a_j)\). If the tail proof passes, this will show that theta’s count sectors take both signs arbitrarily far out. It tests a possible count-sign mechanism; it does not exclude collisions.

One limitation matters: the count probabilities may be extremely small, so normalized sign oscillation alone gives no practical sampling or truncation bound.
